what_it_does: When chip designers build a new processor, they typically maintain two separate programs: a simulation model used to explore design ideas quickly, and a chip blueprint (called RTL — a low-level hardware description language that tells fabrication tools exactly how to wire up the transistors) used to actually build the chip. Keeping these two in sync is tedious and error-prone. Assassyn lets designers write a single program using a familiar concept — asynchronous events (like callbacks in software) — and automatically compiles it into both a cycle-accurate simulator (for design exploration) and synthesizable RTL (for manufacture). Because both outputs come from the same source, they are guaranteed to describe the same architecture, eliminating the alignment errors that arise from dual-codebase maintenance.
